result.title: An Incremental Knowledge-Graph Learner Digital Twin for Evidence-Grounded Early Warning
result.summary: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. A risk score may indicate that intervention is needed without showing which traces, assessment events, or temporal patterns justify the alert. This paper introduces an incremental Learner Digital Twin for evidence-grounded early warning, implemented as a lightweight knowledge graph. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. The framework is instantiated and evaluated on a public learning-analytics benchmark under a temporal protocol. The results show that graph-mediated feature extraction preserves the predictive behavior of equivalent raw-table features across model families and checkpoints. Generated alerts are materialized as evidence chains linking risk decisions to feature attributions, evidence items, and raw platform records. The study shows that early-warning prediction can be routed through a semantic and provenance-aware representation while preserving predictive performance and adding traceability, verifiability, and evidence-grounded explanation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出用轻量知识图谱实现的增量「学习者数字孪生」：在时间检查点重放学习轨迹与测评记录，把特征、归因、告警、证据条目和原始记录都落成可查询图实体，并以图查询抽取预测特征，在学习分析基准上按时间协议评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把风险决策与特征归因、证据条目、原始记录串联成可查证据链、并在检查点增量更新状态的做法，可能为 LVR 中「证据筛选—归因—答案」的可核查评价提供线索；但任务与模态都与视觉推理相距较远，借鉴性需核查。
